title: Deion Sanders leads Colorado to first top-15 win since 2007: Coach Prime cools hot seat talk ... for now - CBS Sports
description: Sanders and the Buffaloes picked up one of the program's biggest wins in nearly 20 years in an upset over Houston
body:
Sanders and the Buffaloes picked up one of the program's biggest wins in nearly 20 years in an upset over Houston
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 14, 2026

    12:19 pm ET

            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Colorado Buffaloes picked up its biggest win in nearly two decades on Friday night, stunning No. 14 Houston in a 42-32 victory that ends the Cougars' dreams of a College Football Playoff berth. It's the first time Colorado has beaten a top-15 ranked team since 2007 and gets the Buffaloes to 4-6 -- guaranteeing an improvement over last year's 3-9 campaign. It's a massive win for Deion Sanders in his fourth year at the program, as he's been desperate for his team to show that kind of performance against a quality opponent. The hot seat chatter around Sanders has been growing for the past two seasons. Last year's 3-9 effort saw a massive drop-off after the 9-4 season with Heisman winner Travis Hunter and Shedeur Sanders leading the way. Life without Hunter and Sanders has been rough for the Buffaloes, and Coach Prime has been struggling to prove that he can build something in Boulder without those two stars. Friday night's win over Houston offered a chance to exhale, both for Sanders and Colorado fans, who seemed resigned to their fate of having another year at the bottom of the Big 12 with no clear exit strategy in sight. For as much conversation as there's been about whether the Buffaloes should move on from Sanders, the financial reality made it extremely difficult -- if not outright impossible -- for the school to end the Coach Prime tenure. 
Sanders received a massive extension after that 9-4 campaign in 2024 and would be owed $25.5 million if he were fired after the 2026 season. That's not money Colorado has tucked away in a rainy-day fund, and the Buffaloes needed Sanders to be the one to decide to walk away. That has seemed unlikely, as he's insisted he's the right man for the job and capable of turning things around. But until Friday night, he was without a proof point of progress being made. Sanders insisted his team was showing all the right things in practice and doing all the right things off the field. But what matters to fans is what shows up on the field on Saturdays (or Friday nights), and up until Nov. 13, Colorado had yet to make a real statement. The Buffaloes had close calls, like a 27-24 loss at home to a Utah team that's currently No. 2 in the nation. That offered a glimpse of what's possible, but there have been too many losses in Boulder for Sanders to point to moral victories in defeat. 
Friday's win over Houston was exactly what he needed to at least cool down the temperature in Boulder and buy himself a bit more goodwill ahead of his fifth year in charge. The Buffaloes likely were going to stick with Sanders either way because of the finances, but it becomes a much easier pitch to fans to support the team entering Year 5 with a win over a playoff contender.

        Jeremiah Smith has rewritten the record books a lot throughout his three seasons at Ohio State, and he just broke a record that stood for 23 years on Saturday. With his 22-yard reception in the first quarter against Northwestern, Smith is now the Big Ten's all-time leader in receiving yards.Smith entered the day trailing Purdue receiver John Standeford, who set the record with 3,788 career yards in 2003. Since then, great receivers have come and gone in the Big Ten, but none have sniffed Standeford's record.That is, until Saturday, when Smith finally passed him. The historic play came late in the first quarter when freshman quarterback Luke Fahey found Smith running free over the middle of the field for a 22-yard gain.
The list of records that Smith owns only continues to grow -- at the NCAA, school and conference levels. Oh, and he still has at least two more games left in him.
NCAA -- Freshman receiving yards (1,315)NCAA -- Freshman receiving touchdowns (15)Big Ten -- Career receptions (232)Big Ten -- Career receiving touchdowns (41)Big Ten -- Career receiving yards (3,798)Ohio State -- Most 100-yard games (16)Ohio State -- Single-game receiving touchdowns (4)The question now is whether Smith will cap his incredible career with the greatest individual honor in college football. An injury to Miami wide receiver Malachi Toney has opened the door wide open for Smith to make a serious push. If he continues to tear up the stat sheet in the final three weeks, Smith may hear his name called in New York.In fact, Smith is now the favorite to win the award at +150, according to FanDuel Sportsbook. Darian Mensah (+340) and C.J. Carr (+370) are the only other players even close to the Buckeyes superstar.
Even if Smith falls short of the award, due largely to the injury to starting quarterback Julian Sayin, he will have a lasting legacy in college football. He's set the bar high for any receivers trying to chase him down in the future.

        A pair of title fights are set for Saturday when UFC 334 goes down at Madison Square Garden in New York. In the main event, Ciryl Gane will make his first defense of the UFC heavyweight championship when he takes on rising star Josh Hokit. Plus, women's bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison and women's GOAT Amanda Nunes look to settle their rivalry in a bout nearly a year in the making.Gane became champ after earning the interim strap with a win over Alex Pereira at UFC Freedom 250 in June. He was elevated to full champ when Tom Aspinall vacated the title due to lingering eye injuries.Hokit, meanwhile, is looking to complete one of the fastest rises to championship status ever after making his promotional debut in November 2025. He has a sneaky Fighter of the Year resume if he's able to pick up a fourth win this year on Saturday night that would include Curtis Blaydes, Derrick Lewis and Gane.Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC 334 for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!
The co-main event is a title bout years in the making. Women's bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison looks to earn a capstone win to her MMA career over the women's GOAT Amanda Nunes. The two were originally set to fight in January when Harrison suffered a scary neck injury that required surgery. But the wait is finally over. Harrison is one of the most accomplished women's combat athletes of all time with two Olympic gold medals in judo followed by world titles with PFL and now UFC. But Nunes is considered the GOAT for a reason after beating every single champion or former champion of her active competition era.With such an interesting card set for UFC 334, there will no doubt be plenty of interest in the event, including at sportsbooks. With that in mind, we've once again looked at all the event's main card fights to identify our best bets for each.
        
            
                UFC 334: An inside look at Josh Hokit's incredible rise to title challenger in just one year
                
                    Brian Campbell                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
After a strong 4-1 result for our best bets for UFC 333, we are sitting just under .500 at 27-29 for the year. Now we look ahead to this weekend with the goal of getting back in the black, with our only rule remaining that all bets must be at odds of -250 or better. Let's take a look at this week's picks with odds via DraftKings Sportsbook.  
Bilal Hasan	vs.	Luis GuruleUnder 1.5 rounds (-175)Bilal Hasan is a pretty massive -1200 favorite and is even -800 at -3.5 on the point spread line. After an impressive showing on Dana White's Contender Series and a knockout in his UFC debut, it's pretty clear that Hasan's being given another chance to impress when he faces Luis Gurule, who is 1-4 since his own appearance on Contender Series. Roughly a quarter of flyweight non-title fights end before the midway point of the second round. Hasan scored one of those early stoppages in his first UFC fight, but that win came at the 2:28 mark of Round 2, coming in just two seconds on the "under" side. Gurule has had a rough go of it in the UFC, and this fight is set up to continue Hasan's rise, so I'll side with him getting it done quickly.Uros Medic vs.	Kevin HollandUros Medic moneyline (-155)Kevin Holland is one of the trickiest fighters to understand in the game. He can look fantastic using his length and craftiness and also can get dominated by fighters who are dialed in. Holland is 8-10 since 2021, which isn't a great record, but 18 fights since the start of 2021 is a wild career pace. Uros Medic is riding a four-fight knockout streak, most recently taking just 30 seconds to stop Daniel Rodriguez in Serbia. Medic brings big power and a lot of speed, so if he can get inside of Holland's reach, he can likely do some very good work. Medic just needs to stick to the gameplan and not be baited by Holland's antics. If Medic hesitates to move forward, he's in trouble, but I think he has the right style to break Holland down over the course of the fight.Caio Borralho	vs.	Yousri BelgarouiCaio Borralho moneyline (-155)This fight likely comes down to which version of Caio Borralho shows up. Early in his UFC career, we saw Borralho willing to use takedowns and ground control, such as when he scored four takedowns of Armen Petrosyan for more than 10 minutes of control time. Borralho only has one takedown in his five most recent fights. Both styles have worked well for Borralho, who has an 8-1 UFC record, but against Yousri Belgaroui, Borralho will have a far easier time finding his old takedown and ground game style. Belgaroui is a fantastic kickboxer, who has blitzed his UFC competition so far. Even in finding success on the feet, Belgaroui has been taken down plenty in his short UFC career and Borralho is a good enough fighter to take advantage of that skill gap to find a win.
Kayla Harrison vs.	Amanda NunesOver 3.5 rounds (+105)Every now and then, you get a fight where the best you can say is, "Man, I don't know." Nunes might be impacted by rust from the time since her retirement. Harrison might also be a bit rusty in recovering from neck surgery. There's no real way to know how those issues factor into how things play out. I lean toward this fight stretching on for a while, however, with both women being a bit out of form and likely cautious of what the other brings to the cage. Harrison will want to score some takedowns and I think she can hold Nunes down, but maybe not find a finish. Around the third round, I expect both women to show some fatigue and things could get a little ugly. I think things are set up to get into the late stages, so I'll go with the over.Ciryl Gane vs.	Josh HokitCiryl Gane moneyline (-205)Hokit's rise has been admirable, whatever you feel about his behavior outside of the fight. But this is a big jump for him. Gane has been susceptible to takedowns in the past, most notably against Jon Jones and Francis Ngannou. The Ngannou fight is more of a red flag than getting taken down by Jones, but that fight also took place almost five years ago and I think Gane has improved plenty since then. Gane has the size, reach and striking advantage in this fight, so if he can keep from getting taken down, this may be an easy title defense for him. Hokit showed grit and toughness in his war with Curtis Blaydes, but getting into a fight like that against Gane will go badly for him in a hurry. I'm going with the more proven commodity with the better chances of putting out some serious damage in the main event.Who wins Gane vs. Hokit, and how exactly does the fight end? Visit SportsLine now to get detailed picks and analysis from the incomparable expert who is up over $21,000 on his UFC picks since May 2018, and find out.

        The New England Patriots and Detroit Lions are headed to Germany this week. The teams will kick off Sunday's action with a 9:30 a.m. game at Allianz Arena in Munich on Sunday, Nov. 15. The Lions come into the international matchup at 6-2 and are coming off a 19-9 win over the Miami Dolphins. The victory extended their win streak to four games.Detroit's 6-2 record is strong, but because the NFC North is so good, they are currently narrowly in second place in the division, tied record-wise with the Minnesota Vikings. The Patriots story is a bit different, coming off a bad loss to the Green Bay Packers. In the 45-27 defeat, quarterback Drake Maye threw three interceptions, tying him with winless Los Angeles Chargers QB Justin Herbert for most picks in the league (11).The Patriots are 2-2 in their last four games and sit in second place in the AFC East.
Both teams can make big plays, but it's what happens between those big gains that may determine the winner of this matchup between two coaches, Mike Vrabel and Dan Campbell, who tend to be aggressive in their play-calling. Lions vs. Patriots need to knowInjuries: The Patriots will be without CB Carlton Davis III (knee), C/G Ben Brown (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) this week and nine other players are questionable, including WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and S Kevin Byard III (chest). Brown, who has missed the last two weeks and was IR earlier this season, returned to practice this week in a limited capacity. Brown's production in the three games he did play didn't live up to his hype, drawing criticism from fans. If he can play, all eyes will be on him, especially with the team having fewer options in the run game. Defenses: The Lions' defense has improved over the last few weeks, allowing 15.5 points per game in its last four matchups, after being near the bottom of the league in many categories, including yards allowed per game (423.8) in the first four weeks. The Patriots defense got embarrassed last week, with arguably Christian Gonzalez's worst game of his career. New England's defense has allowed the eighth most passing yards per game (231.9). The team does significantly better against the run, landing eighth-best (96.7), right behind the Lions' run defense (94.1). The Lions offense is top 10 in the league, thanks to Jaymyr Gibbs, who already has 847 yards on the ground and will present a challenge for the Patriots. The Lions' pass defense is still at the bottom in terms of yards allowed (260.9), and with the Patriots needing to improve and establish their air game, this would be the chance to try and expose Detroit's weakness.Pass game: The Patriots' passing game pales in comparison to their Week 10 opponent's. Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has 61 receptions for 657 receiving yards, more than the Patriots' top two WRs (DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III) combined. The lack of production is in part due to struggles from quarterback Drake Maye and the absence of a true WR1, with Brown missing most games and the loss of Kayshon Boutte this offseason. St. Brown's mom is from Germany and it will be the first game he plays on German soil, which should only increase his excitement and production.International history: This marks the sixth regular-season game to be held in Germany and the third played in Munich. It marks the final European game of the season. The NFL traveled to Germany last season as well, when the Colts and Falcons met in November at the Olympic Stadium. Detroit Lions president & CEO Rod Wood expressed his excitement to be playing in Germany, saying, "We are thrilled to be playing internationally and specifically in Munich for the 2026 season. As an organization, we have invested greatly in the German market and are excited to play in front of our passionate German fans."Lions vs. Patriots where to watchDate: Sunday, Nov. 15 | Time: 9:30 a.m. ETLocation: Allianz Arena (Munich, Germany)TV: Fox | Stream: fubo (free trial available)Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Lions -2.5 (via DraftKings)
Lions vs. Patriots predictionI think the Patriots will make some adjustments from last week and come out stronger in Week 10. This game could really go either way and we will know if the Patriots offense has the juice to win right away, as their first few drives tend to establish the rest of the game. If New England's defense can bounce back and Maye can stop giving the ball away, they can keep themselves in the playoff conversation with a win.  Pick: Patriots 33, Lions 30

title: Why is 46-year-old Ronaldinho returning to soccer with Ravenna, an Italian third division club? - CBS Sports

The former Brazilian star will play his first game with Ravenna this weekend in Italy

        Ronaldinho, one of the greatest footballers of all time, will be back on the pitch on Sunday, Nov. 15, for a historic day. The Brazilian striker, who won the 2005 edition of the Ballon d'Or and played for PSG, Barcelona and AC Milan at the peak of his European career, signed a deal in the summer of 2026 to join the roster of Ravenna, an Italian team currently playing in the third division. Ronaldinho, who played his last professional match in 2015 and will turn 47 next year, is expected to play some minutes in the home derby against Forli, and you can watch it all on Paramount+. But let's break down how and why he's coming back to play after more than a decade and after announcing his retirement in 2018. 
How to watch Ravenna vs. ForliDate: Sunday, Nov. 15 | Time: 11:30 a.m. ETLocation: Stadio Bruno Benelli -- Ravenna, ItalyTV: Paramount+The Ravenna project Ravenna, who have a history of playing in Italy's lower divisions, were acquired in 2024 by Ignazio Cipriani, the nephew of Arrigo Cipriani, the founder of the iconic Harry's Bar in Venice. The Cipriani Group operates high-end restaurants, private members' clubs (Casa Cipriani), luxury hotels, event venues and branded residences across major international cities, such as New York City, London, Monaco, Miami and Dubai. Basically, it is now positioning itself as a global luxury lifestyle and real estate player, rather than simply a restaurant group. 
This is why Cipriani created links with some of the most notable figures in the world: soccer players, politicians, singers, actors and more. When the group entered the world of soccer, it brought in people who had already worked at the highest level of the game, such as former AC Milan sporting director Ariedo Braida, who played a key role alongside former AC Milan CEO Adriano Galliani in building AC Milan's legacy under Silvio Berlusconi's presidency. Braida left AC Milan in 2013 after 27 years.Ravenna's current head coach is Andrea Mandorlini, who spent several years coaching in Serie A and represented Inter as a player between 1984 and 1991. The connection with Ronaldinho, who joined AC Milan in 2008 during Braida's tenure at the club, also involves another key figure at Ravenna: Lorenzo Tonetti, the club's head of external relations. During Ronaldinho's time at AC Milan, Tonetti owned Giannino, a restaurant in Milan that became something of a second home for several of the club's players. It was also a favorite meeting place for Galliani, who famously negotiated several transfer deals within its walls. Curiously, one of the waiters working there at the time was Giuseppe Riso, now one of the best-known agents in soccer, who represents players such as Sandro Tonali, Davide Frattesi and Carlos Augusto.
Why is he coming back?Ronaldinho signed a dual player-investor contract in the summer of 2026. He joined Ravenna with the ultimate aim of scoring one final professional goal while also acquiring an ownership stake in the club. Rather than having him play every week, his deal focuses on global marketing and special appearances in marquee matches, such as the local derby against Forli that will take place on Sunday. Ronaldinho is one of the most notable players in the history of the game. He joined Barcelona in 2003, where he became a global superstar, winning two FIFA World Player of the Year awards, the 2005 Ballon d'Or and the UEFA Champions League in 2006. In 2008, he moved to AC Milan, where he played until 2011. At the international level, he was a key part of Brazil's national team that won the 2002 World Cup. He formally retired in 2018 but played his last-ever football game three years earlier, in 2015.

Need some last-minute advice on how to bet the Week 10 slate? Allow us to be of assistance

        Quarterbacks are the story pretty much every week in the NFL, but Week 10 has several fascinating storylines developing under center. For instance, three are set to make their first career starts on Sunday in rookies Fernando Mendoza and Carson Beck along with second-year quarterback Kyle McCord. On top of that, Kirk Cousins is set to start in his return to Minnesota after being acquired at the trade deadline, as will Jacoby Brissett, who the Ravens dealt for to help cushion the blow of losing Lamar Jackson. As you can see by simply looking at this shakeup at quarterback, the aftermath of the trade deadline is going to have ripple effects that spread through the entire league. Naturally, that adds another element for bettors to consider as they put together their picks for Week 10. To help sort through the madness of the last week, we've put together some last-minute best bets for the slate along with picks for every other game on the docket. Note: Chicago, Denver, Philadelphia, and Tampa Bay are on the bye in Week 10.All lines via DraftKings; All times ETPittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati BengalsSunday, 8:20 p.m. (NBC, Stream: Fubo, try for free)There's arguably no offense hotter right now than the Bengals. Over their four-game winning streak, they've averaged over 35 points per game, and Joe Burrow has been playing at an MVP level. The Cincinnati QB has 18 total touchdowns over this stretch and a 132.0 passer rating. Simply put, they've been a bulldozer. However, I do think it's worth pointing out who they've played over the course of the winning streak: at Dolphins, at Ravens (no Lamar Jackson), vs. Titans and vs. Falcons. Not exactly a murderer's row. Pittsburgh, who beat these Bengals back in Week 3, should provide much more resistance than what they've faced recently. The Steelers defense is tied for the fifth-lowest yards-per-play average (5.0), tied for the fourth-lowest points-per-game allowed (18.0), and tied for the eighth-lowest passer rating allowed (83.3). Meanwhile, Cincinnati's defense is tied for the most yards per rush attempt allowed so far this season (5.0), which sets up Jaylen Warren to continue his ascent as one of the true breakout players of the season. 
On top of this being a potential mismatch for the Bengals going up against this stout Steelers team, their scheduling surrounding this game does them no favors either. While they'll be at home in Week 10, Cincinnati is coming off an international game in Madrid last week. As for the Steelers, they're fresh off their bye week, creating a sizable rest discrepancy. All of this is a recipe for an upset. Projected score: Steelers 27, Bengals 24The pick: Steelers +3.5Carolina Panthers at New Orleans SaintsSunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo, try for free)While their 3-5 records don't exactly scream playoff contenders, first place in the NFC South is on the line in this game. Bryce Young doesn't have the best history going up against the Saints, as the Panthers quarterback is just 1-5 against his division foe in his career. That said, I think there's a window here for him to get a rare victory against New Orleans on Sunday. While his numbers have come down since his stellar start to begin the season, Young started to look more like himself in the loss to Denver, completing 71.7% of his passes to go along with three touchdowns. The Saints secondary is allowing 7.3 yards per attempt so far this season, which is tied for the fifth-highest in the league. Their 99.5 passer rating allowed is also the seventh-highest in the NFL. This isn't as daunting a matchup for Young, who had to face Tampa Bay, Green Bay, and Denver over Carolina's recent three-game losing streak. I like him to rebound here. 
Meanwhile, New Orleans is 1-4 straight-up and 0-5 ATS at home this season, so the Superdome hasn't been too friendly thus far. Projected score: Panthers 24, Saints 21The pick: Panthers +2.5Kansas City Chiefs at Atlanta FalconsSunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+)Similar to what we discussed with Cincinnati, the Falcons do have to play immediately the following week after an international game in Madrid last Sunday. That may only put them further behind the eight ball against a Chiefs team that cruised to a 35-12 win over the Jets last week. Patrick Mahomes did give us all a scare in the midst of that game after injuring his elbow, but it's not serious enough to keep him out of this matchup. Mahomes has thrown five touchdowns and no interceptions over his past two games, but his lack of a downfield threat has been noticeable. He's averaging an NFL-low 5.6 air yards per attempt this season as the Chiefs have really looked for pass catches to put up yards after the catch. Well, they just acquired some help in that regard in Josh Downs, whom they brought in before the deadline in a trade with the Colts. The wideout has a knack for creating separation and now has a capable quarterback to deliver the football to him, so Kansas City could see quick dividends from this addition. That's especially true against a Falcons secondary that was just lit up by the Bengals last week and just traded away star safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars.
Atlanta is also 0-4 straight-up and ATS in its last four games against the AFC. Projected score: Chiefs 26, Falcons 20The pick: Chiefs -3Jacksonville Jaguars at Tennessee TitansSunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo, try for free)While they won't play this weekend, Jacksonville went all-in at the deadline, making trades to acquire Jessie Bates III, Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux to bolster its defense for a potential Super Bowl run. On the flip side, Tennessee traded away pieces, including standout safety Amani Hooker and, going back a couple of weeks, defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. That's a lot of talent being drained from the defense, which doesn't bode well against Trevor Lawrence, who is making a sneaky MVP push. Entering Week 10, his 111.7 passer rating ranks second among quarterbacks who have started at least eight games, only looking up to Burrow. As this double-digit spread suggests, this is a David vs. Goliath matchup, and it's hard to imagine the underdog keeping this thing close. Even before making these trades, Jacksonville's defense was allowing 15.1 points per game (second-best in the NFL) and has also allowed 20 or fewer points in six straight road games. Tony Pollard, who remained with the team through the deadline, has been a bright spot in Tennessee's offense in recent weeks, but could be negated here. The Jaguars are allowing 3.7 yards per carry this season, along with an average of 89.3 rushing yards allowed per game that ranks fifth-lowest in the NFL. 
A blowout is brewing in this matchup in favor of Jacksonville, who is 13-3 ATS over its last 16 games with a +16.3 points per game differential. Projected score: Jaguars 34, Titans 16The pick: Jaguars -10.5Seattle Seahawks at Las Vegas RaidersSunday, 4:05 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+)Welcome to the NFL, Fernando Mendoza. The No. 1 overall pick at the 2026 NFL Draft is set to make his first career start in the aftermath of the Raiders trading Kirk Cousins, who started the first nine games of the year, to Minnesota before the deadline. This will be a baptism by fire for the Indiana product as he'll face off against a Seattle defense that is among the very best in the NFL. The Seahawks are allowing a league-low 244.2 total yards per game entering Week 10, along with an average of 18.0 points per game allowed that is tied for fourth-fewest. That just feels like too tall a mountain to climb for Mendoza right out of the gate. Meanwhile, the Raiders defense won't do their young quarterback any favors. They're currently on a six-game streak of allowing 30-plus points, which is tied for the longest streak within a season all-time. So, even with Sam Darnold (quad) sidelined and backup Drew Lock set to play through an oblique injury, the Seattle offense should find plenty of scoring opportunities. This could be a breakout game for Zach Charbonnet after leading the team with 16 carries last week for 77 yards, as the Raiders are allowing an NFL-high 5.0 yards per carry. 
Given that Mendoza is getting the start, it's also worth pointing out that No. 1 overall quarterbacks are 1-15-1 straight up and 3-14 ATS in their first career starts since 2003. Projected score: Seahawks 30, Raiders 20The pick: Seahawks -6.5Rest of the bunchPatriots at Lions (in Munich)Projected score: Lions 30, Patriots 20The pick: Lions -2.5Bills at JetsProjected score: Bills 33, Jets 21The pick: Bills -8.5Texans at BrownsProjected score: Texans 23, Browns 20The pick: Browns +4.5Dolphins at ColtsProjected score: Colts 27, Dolphins 17The pick: Colts -3.5Vikings at PackersProjected score: Vikings 24, Packers 23The pick: Vikings +2.5Rams at CardinalsProjected score: Rams 27, Cardinals 17The pick: Rams -9.549ers at Cowboys Projected score: 49ers 33, Cowboys 24The pick: 49ers -4.5Chargers at Ravens (Monday)Projected score: Ravens 24, Chargers 17The pick: Ravens -4.5

        UConn began its toughest seven-game stretch of the season Friday. It's a set of games featuring five contests against power-conference opponents projected to make the 2027 NCAA Tournament, four of which are in Saturday morning's updated CBS Sports Top 25 And 1 daily college basketball rankings.On CBS Sports HQ, just before the Huskies tipped against Ohio State, I was asked how I thought UConn would do over this span, one we now know Dan Hurley's team will have to get through without Nik Khamenia, the 6-foot-8 transfer from Duke who suffered a left-foot injury in Monday's win over Wagner.I predicted a 5-2 record for UConn over the next seven games.According to KenPom.com, that would require the Huskies to win at least one contest in this stretch that they're not currently projected to win -- either at Arizona on Wednesday or against Duke a week later or against Illinois on Dec. 12 in Chicago. It's a big ask, I know. But things did get off to a nice start Friday thanks to an 84-68 win over Ohio State in which Elite Eight hero Braylon Mullins led all scorers with 22 points on a 7-of-13 shooting performance featuring five made 3-pointers.
"We're UConn," Hurley told TNT's Andy Katz after the 16-point victory. "We're UConn. We're dealing with some medical stuff -- [and] not just with Nik. But, you know, we've just got a culture and a mindset."As David Cobb noted in a piece about Khamenia's injury, this is the fourth straight season UConn will have to navigate an extended stretch without an important newcomer. In the previous three years, they've still managed to average 31.7 wins and make two trips to the Final Four, one of which resulted in a national championship. So, as Hurley said, the Huskies have a culture and a mindset, and history suggests that culture and mindset will keep them good even in Khamenia's absence.UConn remains No. 2 in Saturday morning's updated Top 25 And 1 daily college basketball rankings, where Florida is still No. 1 after improving to 4-0 Friday with an 83-54 win over Merrimack. Florida and UConn have combined to win three of the past four national championships. title: Amanda Nunes vows to reclaim her throne at UFC 334 and fight until her body quits: 'I'm here to stay' - CBS Sports

body:
After three years away from the Octagon, Nunes is ready to challenge her former teammate Kayla Harrison on Saturday night

        The more things change, the more they stay the same. Amanda Nunes insists she's not returning to the UFC for one last payday or to relive her glory days. The greatest women's fighter in MMA history wants to pick up right where she left off at UFC 334, taking back the title she never lost and sticking around after.Nunes challenges women's bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison at UFC 334 on Saturday at Madison Square Garden in New York City. It's been three years since Nunes last stepped into the Octagon, retiring at the top of her game as a double champion. She's since watched Harrison emerge as the division's dominant force, setting up a long-awaited showdown between former teammates. Harrison hinted that Saturday's fight could be her last, pointing to Janury's career-threatening neck surgery and demanding weight cuts. Nunes, 38, believes she has plenty to offer despite being the older fighter coming off a three-year retirement.Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC 334 for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!
"I'm here to stay. I'm a fighter, man. This is a huge difference between me and Kayla. She's an athlete. I'm a fighter," Nunes told CBS Sports' Brian Campbell. "I'm here to get the belt and fight until my body tells me to stop again. So I'm a fighter. I'm the UFC champion. You're not here with the challenger. You don't talk to the challenger. You talk to a double champion. I know everything that Kayla's going through right now because, for so long, I did this in two divisions. I know everything that she's going through right now. Every single thought, every single mindset, everything."
Nunes knows what it takes to be a champion more than most. She spent years ruling the UFC women's bantamweight and featherweight divisions, defeating fellow greats like Ronda Rousey, Cris Cyborg, Valentina Shevchenko (twice) and Holly Holm. By the time she retired in 2023, there was virtually nothing left for her to accomplish. Harrison's arrival in the UFC gave Nunes a convincing reason to comeback.Her return required patience. Nunes and Harrison were originally scheduled to fight in January before the matchup was pushed back to November. The delay disrupted Nunes' plans, but she sees the upside in having more time to prepare for her first fight in three years.
"Honestly, I keep everything in a positive way," Nunes said. "So I always wait for a little while, and that extra time gives me extra training. So I enjoy a lot being able to add more things and fixing more things. I obviously was a little upset because I always have a plan after fights. I want to go to Brazil. I want to see my family. But when I got home, I was like, 'all right, this is not that bad.'"Nunes' return is a sigh of relief for women's MMA. The sport's biggest stars have gradually stepped away, and the bantamweight division has struggled to produce new attractions of comparable stature. Harrison, a two-time Olympic gold medalist in judo, is among the exceptions. Nunes believes their fight can restore some of the interest that surrounded women's MMA during her championship reigns."This is what women's MMA needs right now," Nunes said. "I feel like it slowed down a little bit, and I'm coming back to make this hype again. I feel like the 135 division needed me. I came back, and I did it for that, and I did it for myself. I was missing this so much. I can't even explain in words how I missed fighting. 
"When I saw that Kayla signed with UFC back then, I told everybody she had a chance to get his belt, and that would be perfect. So I'm coming back to get the belt from her. So now we are here to fight in amazing New York. It's all full cycle in my life."New York is an especially fitting setting for Nunes' revival. Nunes originally arrived in the United States from Brazil with little money and enormous ambitions. Her first stop was New York, where she slept on a gym floor while trying to establish herself as a professional fighter."I was 20 years old when I came to USA, and the first place was here in New York. [I had] $20 in my pocket, and I was sleeping at the gym in Patterson," Nunes said. "When I came here, I dreamed of everything. 'Maybe one day.' I put it out there that maybe I'm going to have my pictures all over, and maybe fighting one day. That would be great. Now I'm 38 years old."
Nune risks a small blow to her legacy against a younger champion who has spent the last three years competing while Nunes enjoyed retirement. Some 41 months have passed between Nunes' last fight and her next. Legitimate questions remain about whether the former champion can regain her old form, particularly against a physically imposing grappler like Harrison. Nunes, however, is pleasantly surprised by how naturally she settled back into training."I feel like 20, honestly. I feel so good. I didn't expect to feel like that," Nunes said. "So everything is coming together perfect. The training. Everything [feels] like I never left this game. It is unbelievable."For all her accomplishments, Nunes enters Saturday's fight as a betting underdog. It's a position she's rarely experienced over the last decade. The last time oddsmakers picked against her was before she knocked out Cyborg in 51 seconds. It's a reasonable reflection of the circumstances. Harrison has been active, while Nunes is attempting a comeback at an age when most fighters are well into their decline.
Nunes isn't bothered by it. She spent the early years of her career proving people wrong and sees another opportunity to do so against Harrison. That chip on her shoulder is particularly visible from the opposite corner. Nunes' former coaches at American Top Team will be in Harrison's corner on Saturday. Nunes relishes the opportunity to best the team she believes didn't have her best interests in mind."Honestly, like this is like my entire life," Nunes said. "I have always been the underdog. So I take that as a motivator, you know, positive. I like to be the underdog. I don't have any problem with that. I'm ready for anything that Kayla shows up on Saturday, and I'm not dying in my mind. I'm going to walk away with my belt, and I'm going to defend my belt."Who wins Gane vs. Hokit, and how exactly does the fight end? title: MLB rumors: Blue Jays targeting Ketel Marte, Giants rejecting calls for Logan Webb - CBS Sports
description: Here are the latest news and rumors from the MLB hot stove on Saturday, Nov. 14
body:
Here are the latest news and rumors from the MLB hot stove on Saturday, Nov. 14
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:52 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The annual GM Meetings came and went this week with two significant transactions. The Braves signed reliever Evan Phillips (three years and $35 million) and the Red Sox signed slugger Jake Bauers (four years and $58 million). Bauers will give Boston some sorely needed home run power. Phillips will pair with Robert Suarez in the late innings for Atlanta.  Otherwise, the GM Meetings brought a lot of rumors and presumably the groundwork was laid for moves that could be completed later this offseason. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Saturday's hot stove happenings.   
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Blue Jays have interest in Marte
The Blue Jays have interest in Diamondbacks second baseman Ketel Marte, who has a full no-trade protection, reports Sportsnet. It does not appear a trade is imminent. We ranked Marte among the offseason's top trade candidates despite his odd AWOL incidents the last few seasons. Even at 33, he remains one of the game's best second basemen.The Blue Jays went 79-83 this past season largely because of their offense, which ranked dead last in runs and home runs. They also ranked 17th in WAR at second base as All-Star Ernie Clement ran out of steam in the second half. Offensively, Marte is coming off his worst 162-game season since 2018, though he would still represent a clear upgrade for the Blue Jays.

                            
    
                                                
                    
      Giants continue to decline calls about Webb  
The Giants continue to decline trade calls about ace righty Logan Webb, reports USA Today. Webb, 30 next week, had his worst full season in the big leagues in 2026, in part due to a nagging knee injury, though he is signed affordably through 2028. San Francisco needs to add to its rotation, not subtract one of the game's best and most durable starters.  That said, a Webb trade would presumably net the Giants multiple young players and improve the team's talent base. It never hurts to listen, but for now, the Giants seem disinclined to move their best pitcher since Madison Bumgarner was in his prime. Webb and Landen Roupp are the only locks for San Francisco's 2027 rotation at the moment.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
      Braves looking to add a starter  Not surprisingly, the Braves want to add at least one starting pitcher, according to The Athletic. They could also re-sign Raisel Iglesias or bring in another late-inning reliever even after signing Phillips. Chris Sale and Grant Holmes are Atlanta's only returning healthy starters. Bryce Elder (knee), Spencer Schwellenbach (elbow) and Spencer Strider (elbow) all finished the season injured.  
The Braves will give Didier Fuentes, who was so dominant as a reliever this past season, a chance to start in 2027. It will be difficult to count on him for a full season, however. Fuentes, 21, threw a career-high 97 innings between the minors, majors, and postseason in 2026. Atlanta will need to monitor his workload next year. Another starter to soak up innings is a must this offseason.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
      Tigers interested in Imanaga  
The Tigers have interest in free agent left-hander Shota Imanaga, reports MLB.com. Jackson Jobe, Troy Melton, River Ryan, and Framber Valdez are presumably locks for Detroit's rotation. Ty Madden and Keider Montero are depth options. Reese Olson is expected back from shoulder surgery early next year. Still, the Tigers could clearly use another starting pitcher.  We ranked Imanaga, 33, as the 30th-best free agent available this offseason. He has been very home run prone the last two years (1.9 homers per nine innings), which could make him a good match for what is now called Fifth Third Park. Detroit's stadium tends to play pitcher-friendly, particularly in April and September (and October), when the ball doesn't carry well in the cold.  

                            
    
                                                
                    
      Blue Jays getting calls about Clement, Schneider  
The Blue Jays are receiving calls about infielder Ernie Clement and utility man Davis Schneider, reports The Athletic. Teams have also inquired about catcher Brandon Valenzuela, who was a Gold Glove finalist as a rookie in 2026. Toronto reportedly has interest in Jazz Chisholm Jr. as it seeks more of a power bat on the infield, potentially making Clement expendable.  Schneider, 27, had a poor 2026 and spent time in Triple-A, though he is versatile and has hit lefties in spots over the years. There is a shocking shortage of quality right-handed bats throughout baseball right now. Schneider's heavy plate discipline approach and ability to play left field as well as some infield positions make him an interesting enough target this offseason.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
      Cubs, Padres, White Sox pursuing Taira  The Cubs, Padres, and White Sox are among several teams pursuing Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, reports the San Diego Union-Tribune. Taira, 26, had a 1.36 ERA in 145 innings for the Seibu Lions in 2026. We ranked him as the 19th-best free agent available this offseason, though he could ultimately wind up in the bullpen given his height (5-foot-8).  
The Padres and two Chicago teams need starting pitching this offseason (they need multiple starters, really) and would likely use Taira in their rotation, at least to begin the season. For what it's worth, Taira told Sanspo he does not have a preferred destination, geographically. The Cubs, Padres, and White Sox would all give him a chance to pitch for a contender right away.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
      Cardinals won't move Burleson, Winn  
The Cardinals have declined trade inquiries into first baseman Alec Burleson and shortstop Masyn Winn, according to the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. St. Louis is also receiving interest in catchers Jimmy Crooks and Pedro Pagés, who are more likely to be traded. Burleson and Winn are off-limits, though, and considered part of the long-term future in St. Louis.  Leo Bernal, who was so impressive during his September call up, and top prospect Rainiel Rodriguez are the future behind the plate for the Cardinals. Pagés is a traditional glove-first backup catcher. Crooks has some offensive upside thanks to his hard-hit ability (exit velocity, etc.), and he rates well as a pitch-framer and thrower. He's an appealing target for catcher-needy teams.

        The NFL won't be the only show in town on Sunday afternoon. Thanks to a nationwide ground stoppage issued by the FAA on Friday afternoon, the SEC matchup between No. 19 Ole Miss and Oklahoma has been moved to Sunday.When the stoppage was announced, the Rebels hadn't taken off for Norman, and they began evaluating other options for their game against the Sooners. Busing wasn't exactly an option for Ole Miss since it takes roughly eight hours to get from Oxford to Norman, and the originally scheduled kickoff time was at 3:15 p.m. CT.By the time the FAA lifted the stoppage late Friday night, Ole Miss didn't want to travel that late and play the following afternoon. As a result, the SEC stepped in and rescheduled the game for 1 p.m. ET on Sunday. The decision didn't go over well with Oklahoma, and athletic director Roger Denny released a statement voicing his displeasure."Put simply, this decision isn't fair to our athletes, our institution or to Sooner Nation," Denny said in a statement released early Saturday. "But we've been given no other choice. We are obligated to play the game when directed, but we remain steadfast in our belief that the wrong outcome was reached this evening."
In spite of the Sooners' objections, the game will be played on Sunday, right as the NFL is kicking off its afternoon slate, and it will be a big one for Ole Miss. If the Rebels want any chance of sneaking into the College Football Playoff as a three-loss team, they have to run the table, which means overcoming travel difficulty and a beat-up running back room to beat Oklahoma.Here is everything you need to know how to watch Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma amidst a sea of NFL action on Sunday.

title: FAA ground stop forces NFL to reshuffle officiating crews for Week 10 - CBS Sports
description: The changes include one referee pulling double-duty on Sunday
body:
The changes include one referee pulling double-duty on Sunday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:42 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL has made several officiating changes for Week 10 in response to Friday's FAA ground stop. Officials have been reassigned to games that are within driving distance of their hometowns.  Among the biggest changes for Sunday will be two referees working games as umpires, three backup referees assigned to work games, four officials working multiple games, and one game without on-site replay officials and assistants. Alex Kemp, who is ordinarily a referee, is going to be an umpire under Clete Blakeman for the Packers' home game against the Vikings. Carl Cheffers, who is also ordinarily a referee, is going to be an umpire under Bill Vinovich for the Raiders' home game against Seattle. Backup referees Barry Anderson (umpire), Duane Heydt (umpire) and Don Willard (side judge) will each work as referees on Sunday. Anderson will work the Titans' home game against the Jaguars. Willard, who has never worked as a referee for a regular season game, will work the Colts' home game against the Dolphins before making the nearly two-hour drive to Cincinnati to work the night game between the Bengals and Steelers. Along with Williard, umpire Terry Killens, field judge Jabir Walker and side judge Justin Larrew will also make the road trip from Indianapolis to Pittsburgh to work Sunday night's game in Cincinnati after working the Colts-Dolphins game. This might get interesting if the Colts-Dolphins game goes into overtime, delaying their arrival in Cincinnati. Regardless, it's safe to assume that there will be no shortage of caffeine consumption for this group of officials on Sunday. 
As noted above, the league's replay officials and assistants were also impacted by the ground stop. The result is that the Panthers' home game against the Saints' will not have on-site replay officials and assistants. 
How will all this impact the games? CBS Sports NFL sideline reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala asked a longtime, now-retired NFL official whether these changes will create any specific challenges. According to his response, the first few series may go a long way toward determining how smoothly the rest of the game goes. "He said familiarity and a general crew tempo are real, so we should watch how the officials adjust to each other the first couple series," Kinkhabwala wrote on X. "And while most officials watch film of the teams they have to be aware of tendencies (and won't have time to do so now), he did downplay any impact there, saying it's ultimately all about watching your keys."
The FAA ground stop -- the second since the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks -- resulted in more than 2,000 canceled flights. The stop was later attributed to the addition of new technology to the nation's air traffic control system, which caused "intermittent" communications and radar gaps.

title: What's next for Red Sox after Jake Bauers deal? Plus more intel from the MLB GM Meetings - CBS Sports
description: Boston could move on from once-promising outfielders Kristian Campbell and Jarren Duran this winter
body:
Boston could move on from once-promising outfielders Kristian Campbell and Jarren Duran this winter
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        LAS VEGAS — Uncertainty permeated the ARIA Resort & Casino throughout this week's MLB GM Meetings. The looming lockout, of course, played a major role in all of this. With Dec. 1  approaching, media, executives, and all within the baseball industry had some questions: what would baseball look like once the inevitable lockout goes into place? What will it look like once it returns? How do you build a roster with such indeterminacy? For the Red Sox, a small piece of this peculiar period centers on what to do with former top prospect Kristian Campbell. Tuesday (Nov. 17) is a significant date, marking the deadline for teams to decide which players to protect from the Rule 5 draft by adding them to their 40-man roster. Campbell, who did not appear in a big-league game in 2026, is currently on the 40-man, signing an eight-year $60 million extension just eight games into his 2025 rookie campaign. But after his demotion in late June of that season, Campbell never found his way back to the majors. 
Now, with the lockout upon baseball, according to one source familiar with the situation, Campbell's 40-man spot might be in jeopardy. Boston is weighing the possibility of designating Campbell for assignment. When Craig Breslow, the Sox's president of baseball operations, was asked about that Tuesday, he brushed aside the question."I'm not going to speak to that right now," he said "Kristian's part of our organization. We're really happy about that, and we are invested in doing everything we can to get him to perform like he's capable of." 
Now, if the Red Sox do DFA Campbell, the belief is that he would clear waivers, given his contract and lackluster performance at the minor-league level. Campbell is owed $55 million over the next six seasons, earning $13 million and $16 million over the 2031 and 2032 seasons, respectively. Campbell posted a .256/.383/.380 slash line with eight homers in 462 plate appearances at Triple-A in 2026.
        
            
                How a polarizing hitting approach took over MLB, and what happened when it stopped working for a top prospect
                
                    Julian McWilliams                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Because of those figures, one league executive suggested during the GM Meetings that their club would have no interest in Campbell. The exec took it a step further, confidently suggesting that they couldn't envision any team claiming the outfielder, considering the contract. Hypothetically, if Campbell is DFA'd, the Red Sox would free up a 40-man roster spot. If he clears waivers, Campbell, who has less than a year of MLB service time, would be outrighted to Triple-A Worcester. The Red Sox could then eventually add him back to the 40-man roster once they feel his production is worthy of another promotion to the parent club. 
None of this would provide the Red Sox with any financial relief unless another team were to claim him. Campbell's contract would still count toward their competitive balance tax payroll even if he were removed from the 40-man roster and remained in the minors.The risk-reward of such a move is something the Red Sox will also have to consider. Campbell has already acknowledged losing confidence following his recent struggles at both the major- and minor-league levels."He's got a world of potential," said Breslow. "We saw it in the minor leagues when he was coming up. We saw it in the first part of the season in [2025]. Then I think we started to see it in the second half last year, too, [at Worcester]. I still feel like he has a really bright big-league career ahead of him, and excited to get into spring training and see that manifest on the field." 
Jake Bauers The Red Sox signed Jake Bauers to a four-year, $58 million deal Friday, giving the club another power bat in their lineup. Willson Contreras will continue to anchor first base while Bauers will serve as the primary DH, filling in for Contreras from time to time. Bauers had a breakout season with the Brewers this year, batting .266/.389/.484 with an .874 OPS and 26 homers. The combo of plate discipline and damage in the strike zone intrigued the Red Sox. Furthermore, his ability to lift the ball in the air and use the entire field despite being a lefty gives the Red Sox confidence that he will be productive at Fenway. With Bauers part of the fold, though, Jarren Duran's future with the club is even more murky. The Sox are a heavily left-handed offensive club with Bauers, Wilyer Abreu, Masataka Yoshida, Roman Anthony, and Duran in the mix.
One is likely going to have to go. And Duran, who could earn upwards of $11 million in arbitration next season, appears to be the most likely to be dealt.Even before the Bauers signing, multiple sources suggested during the GM Meetings that both the Red Sox and Duran might be better off parting ways via trade. Naturally, there is some apprehension. "I've been hearing for three years now about the outfield logjam that we have, but the reality is we haven't had all of our outfielders, including Masataka, healthy at the same time," Breslow said. "These things have largely taken care of themselves, unfortunately."
Other notesRangers president of baseball operations Chris Young made it known that his team isn't trying to rebuild entering next season. The Rangers have failed to make the playoffs in the three years following their first-ever World Series title in 2023. Still veterans Corey Seager and Jacob deGrom remain on the trade block for the Rangers as they try to shed high-salary players and retool.When agent Scott Boras was asked if the Reds could keep his client, Elly De La Cruz, Boras responded, "Well, the idea of what ownership does and what they choose to do is that they have to understand how they operate and why they operate," he said. "If I'm going to operate like I did 20 years ago and everybody in my division is operating differently, I'm not going to be able to capitalize the franchise to a level that others have to create an opportunity." The Reds looked promising just a year ago, making the postseason in 2025 for the first time in five years. The Reds have made it known to other teams that they are willing to discuss their starting pitching.Starter Sonny Gray reconciled his grievance with the Red Sox after publicly criticizing his early removal from Game 2 of the Wild Card Series. Gray reached out shortly after his comments that evening. The right-hander would be willing to return to Boston, but the league-wide belief is that he ends up closer to his Nashville home. The Braves, who need starting pitching, are seen as the frontrunner for his services.
